Act as the test sub-agent for this task.

Fix GitHub issue #232 in Moneo. Add behaviour tests for three security guarantees:
1. Chart tooltip labels in components/chat-chart.tsx are HTML-escaped, so a hostile merchant name renders as text.
2. A failed bank connection in app/api/bank/connect/route.ts never logs the JWT, key or token. Use synthetic secrets and capture console output.
3. The IOU proposal loader in lib/ai/iou-actions.ts never returns `payload`.
Each test must fail when you remove its protection (try that, then revert) and must still pass after an internal refactor. Extend existing test files where they fit. Use at most about three vi.mocks per file. Never assert on UI copy.

## RESUME: earlier work may exist
A stopped agent may have left uncommitted work in `C:/Users/mgsuk/.t3/worktrees/Moneo/t3-b0084152-7e47269ec25ed672` (branch `t3/issue-232-security-invariant-tests`). A branch `t3/issue-232-security-tests` also exists.
- Inspect both read-only (`git -C <path> status`/`diff`, `git log origin/main..<branch>`).
- Bring over anything useful into your own checkout, then continue.
- Never modify, reset or delete the old worktree.
- Use your own branch `t3/issue-232-security-checks`, created from current `origin/main`.
- Commit as soon as the earlier work is applied, and after each step.

## Rules
- Read AGENTS.md first and follow it exactly. Read `gh issue view 232 --comments`.
- End each commit message with:
  Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Never kill any process you did not start yourself in this session, verified by its PID.** Never kill by name or command line, because other agents run `npm ci`, builds and servers in parallel.
- If `npm ci` stalls, retry it once with `--prefer-offline`. Run only one install at a time.
- Other agents share the moneo-qa backend and QA port 3100:
  - Never run `npm run qa:reset` or `docker compose -p moneo-qa down`.
  - Never touch the owner's backend (.env, port 3000, project `moneo`).
- Before finishing: `npm test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`. Full-suite 5-second timeouts under machine load in files you didn't touch: report them, don't change them.
- Push and open a PR to `main` (`Closes #232`), ending the body with:
  🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
  Never merge.
- Final line: PR <full URL>, head <SHA>, checks and reviews <state>.

{"body":"Parent tracker: #224

**Priority:** P1 (correctness, security or verification priority).

## Problem and current evidence

The audit identified three security guarantees that need executable coverage: chart tooltip escaping in components/chat-chart.tsx; secret-safe bank connection failures in app/api/bank/connect/route.ts; and excluding proposal payloads from the IOU loader in lib/ai/iou-actions.ts.

## Scope

Exercise hostile merchant/chart labels through the actual escaping/render path; use synthetic secrets and rejected bank calls to verify no JWT, key or token reaches logs; verify the IOU loader returns only permitted fields. Extend existing behaviour tests where possible.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Hostile HTML is rendered as text and cannot execute.
- [ ] Synthetic bank secrets never appear in captured error output.
- [ ] IOU proposal reads do not expose payload fields.
- [ ] Each test fails when its protection is removed and survives internal refactoring.

## Verification and constraints

Reproduce the current behaviour before changing it. Run the smallest relevant check during implementation, then npm test, npm run lint and npm run typecheck; add a build for app/config changes and real QA browser verification for changed user flows. Use only disposable moneo-qa services, synthetic records and mocked paid integrations. Verify source installation and desktop compatibility. Preserve financial history, corrections and undo. Do not add prose or comments in place of a deterministic boundary.

## Delivery

This issue records follow-up work; it does not claim the change is implemented. Recheck current main and #224 before starting, since the audit counts may have changed. Keep the PR focused and link its checks and relevant evidence here.","comments":[],"title":"Protect security invariants previously documented only in comments"}
